title: Guess Steve's secret rule
_map: Secret sorting rule (Y1–2). Big idea: grouping things by properties. Creative: sort the farm animals by his own secret rule; Steve guesses it, then swap.
_story: Steve sorts the farm animals into two hoops with a secret rule. Ismaeel guesses the rule, tests where a new animal goes, then makes his own rule for Steve to guess.
_stepChain: things can be grouped by what they're like → a rule decides the group → guess Steve's rule from its groups → test a new animal → make your own rule

talk.goodAnswer: animals with wings or not (or another rule that fits the groups).

talk.ask: What rule did you make up?
talk.goodAnswer: anything that splits the animals clearly: legs, size, colour, where they live.

handsOn: Tip out a box of toys or Lego. Sort them by a secret rule, and see if a grown-up can guess it. Then swap!

narration.speaker: steve
narration.text: I sorted some animals into two groups, with a secret rule! Shh! Can you work out my rule?

question.onRight: Yes, you cracked it! The bird and the bug can both fly. They have wings!

0.mistake: picked a rule that doesn't fit every animal
0.hint: Check your rule on every animal. Is the bug big?
0.say: The bug is tiny, and the bird is bigger. But they're in the same group! What do they both have? Wings!

2.mistake: picked a rule that doesn't fit every animal
2.hint: Check each one. Is a squirrel a pet? Is a bug?
2.say: The cat and dog are pets. But the squirrel isn't, and it's in the same group! Look at Group A: the bird and bug both have wings.

question.reveal: Group A has wings. Group B doesn't!

narration.text: Here comes a new animal. Splash! A fish!

question.prompt: Which group does the fish go in?
question.onRight: Yes! A fish has fins, not wings. So it goes in Group B!

0.hint: Can a fish fly? Does it have wings?
0.say: A fish has fins for swimming, not wings for flying! So it goes with the animals without wings: Group B.

narration.text: Having wings is something true about an animal. Something true about a thing is called a property. Animals have loads of properties! How many legs. Whether they swim. What they eat. Any property can be a sorting rule!

narration.speaker: steve
narration.text: Now you make a secret rule! Sort some toys, or animals. I bet I can't guess it!

rule.text: Sort things by a property they share.
rule.ask: How did Steve sort the animals? Say it out loud! Then tap the eye.
rule.spoken: You can sort things into groups by a property they share, like having wings. The rule decides where each thing goes.

bonus.prompt: Bonus! Can one animal belong to two groups at once?
bonus.reveal: Yes! With two rules, like has wings, and lays eggs, a hen belongs to both! The hoops can overlap to show that.
